rationale: M59 (#825). Every line below is read off callsite-lines-825.java. java has the same defect class as scala: a `method_invocation` node starts at its RECEIVER, so before this pin every call in a newline-continued chain was stamped with the line the chain opened on (`trim` and `toUpperCase` both claimed line 14, which is `return base`). The line now comes from the invocation's `name` field — the identifier that names the call. The instantiation half is the same rule: `instantiates` takes the line of the type node that NAMES the constructed type, not the statement's line. The forbidRelationships entries are the pre-fix behaviour, so re-introducing the receiver-start line fails the gate instead of passing silently.

forbidRelationships.note: pre-fix: the chain-opening line `return base`; `.trim()` is written on 15
pre-fix: same receiver-start line; `.toUpperCase()` is written on 16
pre-fix: the statement's line `return new StringBuilder()`; the first `.append(n)` is written on 25
